title: Galaxy CEO Buys $9.9M in Stock Following 43.5% Monthly Decline

tickers.name: Galaxy Digital Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The shares of Galaxy climbed 7% in pre-market trading on Friday after the company's chief executive expanded his ownership of the firm. CEO Mike Novogratz bought approximately $9.9 million in shares on Thursday, according to an SEC filing, stating that the purchase reflects his belief that the company's trading price is currently detached from its true valuation.

The investment follows a month in which $GLXY shares fell 43.5%. Novogratz cited the growth of onchain finance and artificial intelligence as primary drivers for the company's long term prospects, specifically pointing to its Helios Phase I project in Texas, which has already leased 800 MW of capacity under long term contracts.

selectedTweets.bestBit: 800 MW is already leased under long-term contract
selectedTweets.text:
The blue wave has weighed on companies like ours. I get it. But let’s not confuse politics with long-term fundamentals.

Finance is moving onchain and demand for AI is exploding. These are generational shifts that will play out across administrations and market cycles.

We’ve spent years building Galaxy to win in both. That includes Texas, where we delivered Helios Phase I on schedule and 800 MW is already leased under long-term contract. We’ve worked with legislators and local communities there for years, and we’ll keep doing that with the new administration. We share the same goals: reliable power, protected water and strong communities.

I see a massive disconnect between where $GLXY trades and what I believe this company is worth. That’s why I’m buying more stock, starting today.

I’m betting on us, big time.
